caption:
A snack vendor outwits a zombie horde.
Seedance 2.5 kept this zombie comedy perfectly deadpan.
prompt:
VIDEO PROMPT — 26 seconds, 16:9 horizontal. Ultra-photorealistic live-action look, like a quirky Korean indie film: shot on a digital cinema camera with 35mm and 50mm lenses, soft natural overcast daylight, muted desaturated teal-grey street tones against warm orange accents, fine film grain. The last third moves indoors to a dim, warm amber-lit basement. Camera feel: calm, steady, mostly locked-off or gently drifting compositions, deadpan comedy timing. Pacing: 10 shots, each 1-5 seconds; the heroine never hurries and never looks scared.

CHARACTERS (identical in every shot):
- THE VENDOR GIRL: Korean young woman, about 19, pale smooth skin, soft round face, calm half-lidded eyes, small pink lips. Shoulder-length wavy pastel-pink bob with wispy curtain bangs, worn loose. Outfit: glossy cropped white puffer jacket (always on, open at the front), white collared shirt, red-white-and-navy striped school bow tie, navy school blazer underneath, navy-and-red tartan pleated mini skirt, navy knee socks, black chunky boots, black gloves. Signature: the bright pink hair and the shiny white puffer — she stays completely unbothered the whole time.
- THE ZOMBIES (3-4 of them): adult Korean men, grey mottled skin, cloudy pale eyes, matted messy dark hair, open groaning mouths, dirty torn brown, grey and charcoal jackets and stained trousers. They lunge stiffly with arms out. No blood, no gore — they are clumsy and comical.
- THE CHILDREN: six Korean kids aged about 6-10 with black hair, in winter coats (maroon puffer vest, navy fleece, grey-green plaid jacket, dark parkas).
- THE BOY: Korean boy, about 9, thick black bowl-cut hair with heavy bangs, navy fleece hoodie over a dark sweater.
- THE OLDER GIRL: Korean teen girl, about 16, long straight black hair, black puffer jacket, black gloves.

LOCATION:
- A quiet, grey old-town Korean street: low weathered concrete buildings with metal roll-down shutters and a rust-stained grey facade with an open doorway and a warmly lit stairwell, vertical shop signboards in red, blue and yellow along the road, wet grey paving-block sidewalk, scattered yellow ginkgo leaves on the ground. No other living pedestrians.
- THE STALL: a small wheeled street-food cart with an orange tarp canopy and clear plastic side sheets, a rusty grey steel body with big spoked wheels, a long cast-iron pastry grill with rows of hinged moulds on wooden handles, a dented aluminium kettle of pale batter, a big aluminium bowl of dark red-bean paste, a wire rack of golden round pastries, a stack of brown kraft paper bags, a sky-blue plastic cooler box on the ground beside it, a small handwritten cardboard price sign hanging from the canopy.
- THE BASEMENT: a dim concrete-walled room with exposed pipes, a grey electrical box on the wall, a closed grey metal door at the back, a long worn wooden table, a red vinyl chair, a stack of colourful folded blankets on the left. Warm amber light.

SHOT 1 (00:00.0-00:02.9) — Cooking through an attack. Medium shot from the front, across the grill, locked-off at chest height. She pours a thin stream of pale batter from the dented aluminium kettle into the hot pastry moulds. A grey-skinned zombie in a brown jacket staggers in from frame left behind her shoulder and grabs at her. Without looking up she drops one shoulder and flips him over her back: his body tumbles head over heels through the left foreground in a motion blur, legs in the air, and disappears below the cart. She calmly sets down the kettle and pulls the bowl of red-bean paste closer.

SHOT 2 (00:02.9-00:06.2) — The cooler dodge. New angle: medium shot from the front-left of the cart, slight low angle, locked-off. She steps to the sky-blue cooler on the ground and lifts its lid. A zombie lurches out of the misty street behind her, arms out, and grabs for her back just as she bends deep into the cooler — his hands close on empty air and he stumbles past. She straightens up holding a white plastic bottle of milk with a blue label, expression unchanged.

SHOT 3 (00:06.2-00:08.2) — The double collision. Wide shot from the road side at knee height, looking past the cart to the street of colourful vertical shop signs. She crouches beside the cooler with the white bottle. Two zombies charge at her from frame left and frame right at the same time; she stays low, and they slam into each other above her head and crumple to the pavement on both sides of her.

SHOT 4 (00:08.2-00:09.0) — Aftermath. Wide frontal shot of the whole cart, locked-off, symmetrical: she walks out from beside the cooler in her boots holding the white bottle and a brown paper bag, stepping between three zombies sprawled face-down on the wet pavement among yellow ginkgo leaves. Behind: the rust-stained grey facade and the warmly lit open stairwell.

SHOT 5 (00:09.0-00:14.5) — Making the pastries. Medium side-angle shot over the grill, camera locked-off at her right side, sidewalk and street in the background. Close detail on her gloved hands: she spoons a mound of dark red-bean paste onto each batter-filled mould, closes the hinged cast-iron mould by its wooden handle, then flips it open to reveal a full tray of round, glossy golden-brown pastries. She holds an open kraft paper bag in her other hand and drops pastries in. MUST SHOW in the background across the sidewalk, out of focus: two zombies stagger, wrestle each other clumsily, and one topples flat onto the paving — she never looks.

SHOT 6 (00:14.5-00:17.5) — Standing still. Wide frontal shot, locked-off, she stands dead centre in front of the cart holding the full paper bag against her chest. Two zombies lunge in from frame left and frame right toward her; at the last instant they crash head-first into each other in front of her and fall away out of both sides of the frame. She does not move or blink. Hold on her standing calmly alone, steam drifting from the grill behind her.

SHOT 7 (00:17.5-00:19.7) — Into the basement. Interior, wide shot from behind the children seated at the long wooden table (their dark heads blurred in the foreground left and right), red chair at the far end. The grey metal door at the back opens; she steps in with the paper bag, turns her back to camera to push the door shut, then turns around and walks toward the table with a small warm smile. Light shifts to warm amber.

SHOT 8 (00:19.7-00:21.9) — Sharing. Over-the-shoulder shot from behind her (white puffer sleeve and pink hair blurred in the left foreground). She sets the paper bag on the table. Around the table six children look up, then lean in excitedly and grab pastries out of the bag, hands reaching from all sides.

SHOT 9 (00:21.9-00:23.4) — First bite. Medium close-up, frontal, locked-off, eye level across the table: the bowl-cut boy holds a golden pastry in a paper sleeve with both hands and takes a big bite, eyes closed; a puff of hot steam rises from the bitten pastry.

SHOT 10 (00:23.4-00:25.8) — Happy ending. Medium two-shot, frontal, across the table, children's heads soft in the foreground: she and the black-haired older girl sit side by side against the concrete wall, each holding a pastry in black-gloved hands, taking bites and chewing. She glances over and breaks into a small satisfied smile. Hold to end.

SOUND: light, quirky, laid-back instrumental beat (soft plucked guitar and brushed drums) running under the whole clip, ending on a warm chord. Street shots: sizzling batter, the clink of the kettle on iron, low zombie groans and gurgles, comical heavy thuds and body flops on pavement, the plastic clack of the cooler lid, the iron mould clanking shut, rustling paper bag. Basement: door creak and click, children's excited giggles and chatter, crunchy bites and contented chewing. No spoken lines.
prompt_short: Photoreal 16:9 deadpan Korean street short: a pink-bob girl in a white puffer calmly cooks red-bean pastries at a grey street cart while clumsy grey zombies crash into each other around her, then shares the pastries with kids in a warm basement.
